item.case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
item.title: Voyager One Against the References

turns.text: Make a silent 9-second widescreen fact clip about Voyager 1, using NASA's mission page as the reference: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-1/ . Three equal-length scenes: 'Launched: September 5, 1977', 'Jupiter flyby: 1979', 'Saturn flyby: 1980'. Keep 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible. Show the probe near Earth, Jupiter, then Saturn; match its real dish-and-boom design. Don't mix in Voyager 2's Uranus or Neptune visits.

item.tests: Tests whether a factual film matches a named reference in dates, mission identity, spacecraft appearance and scene order.

answer_sheet.Facts to include: Voyager 1 launched September 5, 1977, flew by Jupiter in 1979 and flew by Saturn in 1980.
answer_sheet.Length and scene order: 9 seconds total: three 3-second scenes showing Earth, Jupiter and Saturn in that order.
answer_sheet.Wording: Use exactly the five supplied labels. Keep Voyager 1 and Source: NASA Science visible throughout.
answer_sheet.Sound: Completely silent, with no narration, music or sound effects.
answer_sheet.Visual style: Your call, provided the spacecraft matches the real dish-and-boom design and the planets are recognizable.

must_haves: Three scenes appear in order, each lasting approximately three seconds: probe near Earth, near Jupiter, then near Saturn.
Each scene displays its corresponding date caption exactly, with 'Voyager 1' and 'Source: NASA Science' visible throughout.
The probe consistently has Voyager's large circular communications dish and projecting instrument booms, not solar-panel wings or a generic satellite body.
Jupiter is visibly banded and Saturn has prominent rings; neither is replaced with Uranus or Neptune.
The output contains no Uranus or Neptune flyby claims and no conflicting dates.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

style.prompt: Create a silent 9-second 16:9 educational fact clip about VOYAGER 1, with exactly three equal 3-second scenes and hard cuts at 3.0 and 6.0 seconds. No audio, music, narration or sound effects. Reference attribution: NASA Science mission page https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-1/ . Use only the historical facts specified below. Persistent clean white heading 'Voyager 1' at top left for ALL 9 seconds. Persistent readable footer 'Source: NASA Science' at bottom left for ALL 9 seconds. Large crisp, stable, accurately spelled factual captions on dark high-contrast panels in every scene. Scientifically grounded spacecraft visualization, not actual archival footage. Match Voyager 1's real dish-and-boom architecture consistently across all shots: a large white parabolic high-gain antenna dish approximately 3.7 meters in diameter, compact polygonal metallic spacecraft bus behind the dish, gold thermal insulation, a long slender science instrument boom with instruments at its end, an opposing boom carrying three dark cylindrical radioisotope thermoelectric generators, and very long thin magnetometer boom/antenna elements. Not a generic satellite: NO solar panels, NO wings, NO crew cabin, NO rockets or futuristic engines. Keep entire recognizable dish-and-boom silhouette visible, no shape morphing. Scene 1, time 0.0–3.0 seconds: probe in space near Earth, blue curved Earth with white clouds in background, subtle slow camera drift. Exact main caption: 'Launched: September 5, 1977'. This is an illustrative near-Earth launch-era scene, not a rocket launch shot. Scene 2, time 3.0–6.0 seconds: same probe passing near Jupiter, Jupiter's realistic cream and rust cloud bands and Great Red Spot in background; exact main caption: 'Jupiter flyby: 1979'. Scene 3, time 6.0–9.0 seconds: same probe passing near Saturn with realistic pale golden globe and broad thin rings clearly visible; exact main caption: 'Saturn flyby: 1980'. Clear legible typography, restrained cinematic documentary design, realistic relative scale with spacecraft foreground and much larger planet background. Keep the title, footer and each scene caption visible without fades throughout their assigned time. No other captions, no invented facts, no Uranus, no Neptune, no Voyager 2, and no implication Voyager 1 visited Uranus or Neptune. Finish on the Saturn scene at exactly 9 seconds.
